thread:
Maya (Support): FYI - acme reported duplicate POSTs + billing spike after an auth refresh. They say the client retried immediately when the 401 triggered a token refresh and the original request was replayed. Repro steps attached.

Alex (SRE): Can you paste the minimal repro and logs? curious if retries were happening before or after the refresh handshake.

Maya (Support): Logs from the customer (sanitized):
```
REQUEST -> POST /v1/payments 200 OK id=abc123
REQUEST -> POST /v1/payments 401 UNAUTH id=def456
CLIENT   -> refresh token (ok) new_token=tok-xxxx
CLIENT   -> retry POST /v1/payments (no idempotency key) -> 200 OK id=ghi789
```
Customer says they saw two payments for the same intent. They used our JS SDK v1.2.3 with defaults.

Jonah (Client SDK): ugh. Which retry strategy did v1.2.3 use? IIRC we shipped a linear backoff (500ms increments) and auto-replay on auth success for non-idempotent methods. That's noisy.

Maya (Support): Confirmed: default config snippet from their environment: `maxRetries: 4, backoffType: linear, baseDelayMs: 500, retryOn: [429, 503, 500, network_error, auth_refresh]`

Priya (Billing): Duplicate charges are real for idempotent-unprotected endpoints. We need to know if this is a customer SDK issue or server-side hole. If SDK is replaying non-idempotent POSTs after auth, that's likely root cause.

Alex (SRE): Short-term mitigation: support can ask the customer to upgrade to a patched client or set `maxRetries: 0` for payment endpoints. Long-term: we should change SDK defaults to safe behavior.

Jonah (Client SDK): Proposal:
- change default backoff to exponential with full jitter (see: https://www.awsarchitectureblog.com/2015/03/backoff.html)
- do NOT auto-replay non-idempotent methods after auth refresh unless an `Idempotency-Key` header exists
- add explicit opt-in for aggressive retries (customer must opt-in per route)

Example new default pseudocode we want to ship in SDK:
```
retryPolicy = {
  maxRetries: 3,
  backoff: exponentialJitter(baseMs=200, capMs=10000),
  retryOn: [429, 503, network_error],
  replayOnAuthRefresh: false
}
```

Alex (SRE): Agree. Also add telemetry to capture when replay-on-auth would have fired so we can count occurrences and impacted customers.

Priya (Billing): For immediate billing remediation, we can refund affected intents once support confirms duplicates and we can detect same payload/amount within 30s for customer. I'll start the ops refund runbook once support compiles list.

Maya (Support): Repro steps we used with customer: run a script that: 1) send POST /payments with a short-lived token, 2) force token expiry (return 401), 3) client refreshes token and retries same POST. Script included below.
```
# repro.sh (pseudo)
for i in 1..1:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer short-lived" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/payments -d '{"amt":100}'
  # server returns 401 then accept refresh
  # client library will refresh and retry automatically
```

Jonah (Client SDK): I'll open a PR to change defaults and gate the replay behavior behind `replayOnAuthRefresh: false` and add a warning in changelog. I'll also add a configuration option `enforceIdempotencyHeader: true` for payment helpers.

Alex (SRE): Rollout plan:
- patch SDK (Jonah) and cut a 1.2.4 release with default changes and an opt-in flag for legacy behavior
- push docs and migration guide in /docs/sdk/retries (include quick fix: set `maxRetries: 0` for payment calls)
- server-side: short-term: if we detect a replay after auth for a non-idempotent POST, log an anomaly and tag for manual billing review
- QA: simulate heavy auth-refresh + retry pattern to ensure no regression in throughput/backoff logic

Maya (Support): Customer escalated to SEV-2 because of billing impact. Priya to handle refunds, Jonah to send PR by EOD, Alex to add server logging change. I'll keep customer updated.

deploy-bot: deployed new logging patch to staging at 2812350000 :rocket:

Jonah (Client SDK): PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1234 - includes unit tests and migration notes.

Priya (Billing): Confirmed initial refund list prepared. Will need case IDs from support.

Alex (SRE): Follow-up items: add metric `replay_on_auth_detected` and alert if >10 occurrences/hr for any single customer. Also add an entries table in ops dashboard for manual review.

Maya (Support): Thanks all. I'll patch the customer to use the 1.2.4 pre-release and provide them the refund ETA. Will update thread when done. :thumbsup:
